See Here, these are CD rate which are probably the 2nd lowest you can get. Now, lets say you have 500k in saving that you been working on for the last decade or so. Now, with CD rates less 1%, you just be losing money to inflation if you kept any money in a saving account.

During periods of high growth, having a high interest rate is very important as it give the country a line of defence if things go bad economically. If growth suddenly drops, you can drop the interest rate in order to discourage people from saving, and encourage spending, thereby artificially stimulating growth.

Returning to high interest rates brings the reverse problem however, by encouraging more people to save, and discourage people from spending, you regain the defence mechanism at the cost of lessening current economic growth.

The point I'm trying to make is that governments have to pick the right time to raise interest rates as to avoid causing another recession, and given how China has affected American markets recently, we should wait for this situation to play out before taking action.

If you want to simulate growth, actually have a policy where the money flows to the people (huge construction projects, environment projects, etc).
